paper.title_en: Dynamics of Holevo information and negativity for two-qutrit quantum system in a depolarizing channel
paper.abstract_en: This study examines classical information transmission and entanglement dynamics in a two-qutrit system under a depolarizing channel, extending key qubit results to dimension d = 3. We compute the Holevo information and the negativity for a complete family of two-parameter input states defined by Schmidt angles (θ, φ), from separable to maximally entangled. We show that the separable state consistently maximizes Holevo channel information for any depolarizing parameter ς, while the maximally entangled state minimizes it, yielding <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>qutrit</mtext></mrow><mtext>sep</mtext></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ς</mi><mo stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≥</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>qutrit</mtext></mrow><mtext>ent</mtext></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ς</mi><mo stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> over the full parameter space. A threshold ς0 ≈ 0.4 marks a crossover in normalized relative performance, below which the qubit channel achieves a higher normalized Holevo information Id than the qutrit, while above it the qutrit regains its advantage. Negativity reveals entanglement sudden death below a threshold ςc that depends on the Schmidt parameters (θ, φ), with ςc = 0.5 as the specific value for the maximally entangled state. •We extend the entanglement-information trade-off analysis from qubits to qutrits, using a normalized Holevo information to enable a fair dimensionality comparison.•We analyze two-channel scenarios with a qutrit depolarizing noise model and show that entanglement can further degrade the achievable classical Holevo information.•Entanglement sudden death occurs at a critical noise level ςc that depends on the input state parameters for the maximally entangled state.•Higher residual entanglement is associated with reduced Holevo information which reveals a significant anti-correlation between entanglement preservation and information transfer through the channel.
